What if the owners of the site knew that a number of accounts were created by a bot? Would you still feel the same way about that situation?

If it was proven, beyond a shadow-of-a-doubt, that a list of specific accounts, was in fact, 100% created by/for a botnet, yeah... I'd have no problem getting rid of them. But even then, figuring that out is tricky business, and would require a decent amount of proof. And even then, I'd say ban the accounts. After a certain amount of time, if that person hasn't contested the ban and successfully had it reversed, only then delete the accounts after a waiting period of, say, a year.

Deleting accounts is difficult because a lot of legitimate content history may be removed in the process; whether or not it came from a bot or a person. Say a bot posted something genuinely interesting and had hundreds of legit users engage it (comments, up/downvoats, links, saves, cross-posts, etc), would you just delete that account? Maybe you could keep only the content and delete the user account, switching the "submitted by" to [BANNED] or something like that.

But even then, it's tricky trying to figure out which ones to delete and which ones not to. Lots of bot accounts simulate activity on the site in order to mask their intentions until needed, they don't just sit there idly for this exact reason. Which is why just going off and deleting accounts is a pretty terrible idea.

Hey, here's an idea: make an account go into "suspended" mode if no one logs in to it in, say, a year. Then, keep it around for another six months, and notify the user's email (if they registered one) that the count-down timer has started. If they still haven't logged in to the account, then nuke it and do the aforementioned "[BANNED] but keep the content" method. Remove them as mods of any subs they may still be subbed to and send that user an email inviting them to recreate the account in the future if they so please; while also letting them know that, in the interim, someone may come along and take their username and that at this point, it would be out of anyone's control.

Either way, specific protocol would have to be put in place to make the process transparent, fair, and mutually agreed-upon between users and admins. 'cause mishandling the issue of deleting accounts is a pretty good way to start a shitstorm.
